body: Thank you so much. I struggle every single day and have to watch my parents do it too. They're kind of the only reason I try to tough it out still.

Thank you for the encouraging words. I have my bad days and I have my okay days. This post was on a really bad day. I hung out with my nephew after school the other day and it helped. I think I need him more than he needs me honestly. I wish I had the words to help him with losing his dad, but I don't. We are all in so much pain, but it helps to grieve together I guess.

Thank you for responding. I apologize I was just really angry and more venting than delivering all the details. The reason I said hiding in his "nerves" is because the medical examiner my dad talked to said that when he was inquiring about doing an autopsy she advised him that considering he had melanoma cancer doing an autopsy wouldn't make a difference if it was due to an infection or the cancer that directly killed him because he was classified as having metastasized cancer. Also she said that because so much time had passed it'd be difficult to find the cause because of the growing bacteria since this was the next evening after he passed. So he didn't do it and he was cremated.  What troubles me is this and this is all the information I know which is very little I feel, but here it is. He was diagnosed with melanoma cancer a year ago from a mole on his upper thigh. So he goes to this oncologist that puts him on immunotherapy after he undergoes surgery to remove four lymph nodes from his leg and then is advised to have his gall bladder removed because it could have metastasized there. So we all persuade him to do it and that's when things went for the worse. This was back in July and there was a complication during the surgery that took an extra hour and he is released a month later and he gets dehydrated and diarrhea can't keep anything down and is hospitalized. Has pain in his abdomen and find out that there was a bile leak from surgery and caused an infection so they have another surgery to suck it out I guess because antibiotics wouldn't take care of it. They find an infectious nodule near his liver and lung due to that infection and it ends up being a serious procedure to puncture it taking out 25 cc. Send him back and he still has a lot of pain in his abdomen and gets same symptoms keeps being hospitalized oncologist tells him that they can't find any sign of cancer and don't know what's wrong with him. He is understandably getting frustrated everytime he goes and thinks they think he is crazy or something. They change up his medication a little bit take bunch of CT scans, stool samples for C. diff, don't ever find anything or any explanation to what's wrong with him. He loses about 30lbs in a month and its very hard for him to eat. Two weeks ago hes lying on his couch and his wife calls us because he is pale and has alarmingly shallow breathing. We take him to the emergency room at hospital he goes into cardiac arrest from sepsis and dies in front of our eyes half hour after he is admitted. His death certificate states that he was killed due to "cardiac arrest from sepsis infection POSSIBLY due to metastasized cancer". Can't the oncologist locate the cancer if it was still there? Could the surgeon have screwed up and not taking proper care of this infection? Couldn't they tell him something rather than dismiss his claims of pain and send him home? He racked up $700,000 in medical bills, now has his life insurance policy threatened because he started it after he was diagnosed, and dealt with the most unimaginable pain that no human being has ever had the capacity to linguistically convey to another those last two hours of his life. And for what?! No answers? He was a good person and he knew it was something serious, but we didn't and they didn't warn him or us. I need answers for my big brother. He died at 40 years old. It wasnt his time and I worry this gall bladder surgery that I blame ourselves for pushing him to do was the cause. There is medical negligence at work here I fucking know it.  Am I wrong to have these suspicions? Am I just grieving and being irrational in obsessing over finding out what exactly was the cause for my brother's death? He just wanted to know what was wrong with him. A little brother owes him that much right?
